title: makeGetTrackedFiles/makeIsIgnored do not distinguish a git failure (not a repo …
description:
makeGetTrackedFiles/makeIsIgnored do not distinguish a git failure (not a repo / git absent) from an empty result; a non-repo cwd would silently yield zero tracked files and red the whole gate with false path findings. This is an impossible scenario for a check:all build gate (always run inside the repo), so per Simplicity-First no handling is warranted, but worth a comment if the script is ever reused out of context.

Source: cam/issue-61
Review round: 3

suggestion-fingerprint: 3a77c1c059a1

acceptanceCriteria: makeGetTrackedFiles (scripts/validate-agents-md.ts) throws a clear Error (e.g. 'not a git repository / git unavailable') when the git ls-files spawn exits with a non-zero status, instead of returning an empty tracked-files set. A legitimately-empty git repo (exit 0, empty stdout) still returns an empty list without throwing.
makeIsIgnored (scripts/validate-agents-md.ts) throws a clear Error when git check-ignore exits 128, while preserving exit 0 -> ignored (true) and exit 1 -> not-ignored (false).

New tests in test/validate-agents-md.test.ts: makeGetTrackedFiles run against a non-repo cwd throws; makeIsIgnored against a non-repo cwd (exit 128) throws; the existing legit-empty and normal-path behaviours stay green.
The error messages match the existing plain `throw new Error(...)` convention used in scripts/generate-embedded-vendor.ts and scripts/preview-screens.ts (no custom error class).
bun run typecheck, bun test, and bun run check:all all pass green (gate #12 self-check unaffected in the normal in-repo path).
spec.scope: Fail-loud hardening of the two git-plumbing helpers in scripts/validate-agents-md.ts (the CAM-61 doc-as-code gate #12) so a git failure (non-repo cwd / git absent) raises a clear error instead of silently yielding zero tracked files and reding the gate with false path-missing findings. The exit status is already captured in the spawnSync result and currently discarded; the fix inspects it. NOT a live bug: the only caller (check:all / the check:agents alias) always runs inside the repo, so this is defense-in-depth against manual runs or future callers. Out of scope: hardening the identical smell in scripts/ratchet-diff.ts:52-59 (a separate gate, no shared primitive; noted as an optional tiny follow-up, not included here).
gotchas: A legitimately-empty git repo exits 0 with empty stdout, while a non-repo exits 128; a plain `status !== 0` check in makeGetTrackedFiles cleanly separates the error from a legit-empty tracked list (verified) - do NOT reject empty stdout itself.
git check-ignore -q has three exit codes: 0 = ignored, 1 = NOT ignored (normal), 128 = error/not-a-repo. Only 128 should throw; do not throw on 1.

makeIsIgnored's current exit-1/exit-128 conflation is harmless (both decline to exempt), so the false-findings damage comes solely from makeGetTrackedFiles returning empty; both are hardened for clarity but the tracked-files one is the load-bearing fix.
The functions are already exported and used by the real-git regression blocks in the test file, so the fail-loud cases need no production wiring change to test.
